verdicts.evidence: An executed numerical audit on a 99×100 grid checks the supporting-score identity for L1, L2, and KL, yielding max oracle identity error of 0 and max supporting-plane violation of 1.11e-16, confirming the constant 1-alpha predictor is unbeatable under perfect conditional coverage.

The logbook only re-aggregates the authors' official results.csv (not a fresh run) and obtains 68.929% and 33.671%, which do not match the paper's claimed 68.4% and 38.3%; the discrepancy is unexplained and no independent experiment was executed.

An independent synthetic experiment on the paper's 8D heteroscedastic model shows L1-ERT recovering 92% of the analytic violation (0.0866 vs 0.0948) at 30,000 test points, while unaligned CovGap recovers only 5% (0.0049), with oracle-group CovGap bounding the comparison at 0.0953.

The same 30,000-point synthetic run estimates over-coverage at 0.0445 (analytic 0.0460) and under-coverage at 0.0464 (analytic 0.0488), both nonzero and close to theory, demonstrating the asymmetric decomposition.

The logbook only reads the authors' released classification CSV (80 rows) and checks the additive identity and divergence of directional components; no image classifiers were trained or evaluated independently, so this is a data audit rather than an executed experiment.

A controlled experiment with 20 seeds and 5 folds shows a label memorizer produces false in-sample L2-ERT of 0.08886, cross-fitted null ERT of 0, and cross-fitted signal ERT of 0.01013, with zero train/evaluation overlap, directly demonstrating that k-fold cross-fitting removes overfitting artifacts while preserving genuine signals.

overall: The logbook provides independent experimental or numerical evidence for claims 1, 3, 4, and 6, with concrete numbers supporting each. Claims 2 and 5 rely solely on replaying the authors' released output files rather than executing fresh experiments, and the replayed numbers for claim 2 do not match the paper's reported values.
